object_description: two near-identical volumes pushed together at a corner
design_condition: Two near-identical volumes are loosely arranged around the existing school, spanning connected planted outdoor areas and adapting ancillary spaces to the site’s slope.

positive.statement: The outdoor areas span an arch to the existing school building.
The location and separation of the entrances keep the building entrances clear along the street.
The small multi-purpose hall can be converted into a foyer extension and functions as a spacious entrance.
The staircase to the cloakrooms is architecturally appealing and appropriately designed for school sports.
The lighting of the adjoining rooms is otherwise above average.
The ground-floor kindergartens are oriented south and have a visual relationship with the common playground.
The continuous planted band connects the new buildings with the existing school building.
The large sports and playing fields correspond to the loose setting of the two buildings.
The chosen construction method can be assumed to be sustainable.
The facade design and loose setting are appropriate to the village context.

negative.statement: Simultaneous occupancy of the large and small multi-purpose halls is not possible.
The double hall is lit only through a high opening on the north side, producing an uneven distribution of light.
The location and separation of the second staircase required for fire safety are undecided and obscure the floor-plan organization.
The delivery route crosses the access area, creating conflicts during events.
The new buildings are expected to have low construction costs, but their maintenance costs are comparatively high.
The wide central zone and sometimes large classroom depths make the building dimensions questionable for school use and create unsatisfactory daylight situations.
